feedback: [OWNERSHIP_PATH] gen:IMO_111_ShipShape/sh:sparql: The constraint models tank type, capacity, and separation as properties directly on the ship and tests a single ship-level capacity/separation pair. It cannot enforce the requirement for each specified tank, and it can incorrectly pass when one qualifying tank is compliant while another is not or when values from different tanks are paired. Required change: Model tanks as ship-owned components through the canonical component path and evaluate each qualifying tank independently, requiring every oil-residue or oily-bilge-water holding tank with capacity greater than 30 m3 to have separation at least 0.76 m. | [CANONICAL_VOCABULARY] gen:IMO_111_ShipShape/sh:sparql, FILTER(?tankType = "oil_residue_tank" || ?tankType = "oily_bilge_water_holding_tank"): The candidate uses alias strings as tank-type values, although the scoped vocabulary provides canonical tank classes oilResidueTank and oilyBilgeWaterHoldingTank for identifying those tank components. Required change: Identify qualifying tank components with the canonical class terms nltl:oilResidueTank and nltl:oilyBilgeWaterHoldingTank instead of comparing tankType to noncanonical string literals.

current_issues.problem: The constraint models tank type, capacity, and separation as properties directly on the ship and tests a single ship-level capacity/separation pair. It cannot enforce the requirement for each specified tank, and it can incorrectly pass when one qualifying tank is compliant while another is not or when values from different tanks are paired.
current_issues.required_change: Model tanks as ship-owned components through the canonical component path and evaluate each qualifying tank independently, requiring every oil-residue or oily-bilge-water holding tank with capacity greater than 30 m3 to have separation at least 0.76 m.
current_issues.regression_guard: Preserve ship ownership while enforcing the condition per individual tank rather than per ship-level value pair.

feedback: [APPLICABILITY] MainShape/sh:sparql/sh:select: The applicability condition requires only that nltl:tankType exists, but never restricts its value to the two required tank categories; instead it tests unrelated rdf:type assertions. A tank with an arbitrary tankType value can therefore be treated as applicable, while a required tank lacking that extra property can be skipped. Required change: Encode the tank-type applicability directly through the canonical nltl:tankType representation, explicitly limiting it to oil residue tanks and oily bilge water holding tanks, and remove the unconstrained existence check and unrelated substitute classification. Locked resolution: use exactly https://w3id.org/nltl/vocab#tankType. | [MISSING_VALUE_BEHAVIOR] MainShape/sh:sparql/sh:select: The mandatory nltl:individualTankCapacity and quantity-value triples are required for the SPARQL solution to exist, so a relevant tank with missing capacity is silently ignored rather than producing a conformance failure or an explicit incomplete-input result. Required change: Ensure each applicable tank cannot bypass validation when its individual capacity is absent or unusable; enforce the required capacity input before evaluating the >30 m3 exception.
